sourcedFrom: BANISH 22 OWNER'S MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision or edition statement is printed in the document; the cached file is the 2025 posting. (ABSENT — no copyright line printed.)
cleanIntro: A rimfire can is the one suppressor that has to come apart on a schedule rather than when something feels wrong. Unjacketed .22 bullets throw lead, the lead lands with the carbon, and left long enough the two weld the baffle stack into one piece — after which nothing you own will get it apart. BANISH puts a number on it: every 100 to 200 rounds.

steps.title: Host unloaded and open before the can is touched
steps.action: Magazine out, bolt or slide locked back, then look INTO the chamber and put a finger in it. Then the safety. A can comes off the muzzle of a loaded gun more often than anybody admits, and this is the sequence that stops it.
steps.aside: Visually and physically inspect the chamber to ensure the firearm is empty and unloaded. Engage the safety.
steps.quote: Remove the magazine from the firearm, retract the bolt or slide and lock it open.
steps.cite: BANISH 22 OWNER'S MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision or edition statement is printed in the document; the cached file is the 2025 posting. — INSTALLATION OF SUPPRESSOR, printed p.5

steps.title: ⛔ Let it cool, then unscrew it off the muzzle
steps.action: Give it time, or use a cover or a glove. A .22 can after a brick of ammunition will still take skin off. Unscrew it off the threads with the action still open and clear.
steps.aside: When removing the silencer, use extreme caution as it may be hot to the touch after firing.
steps.quote: Before removing the silencer from the host firearm, be sure that the firearm is unloaded, and the action is opened so that it is visibly clear of any ammunition.
steps.cite: BANISH 22 OWNER'S MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision or edition statement is printed in the document; the cached file is the 2025 posting. — WARNING, printed p.2-3

steps.title: Muzzle cap off with the tool key, then the breach cap
steps.action: The key that shipped with the can is the tool for both ends — the muzzle cap first, then the breach cap off the other end. Nothing here is torqued; if a cap will not start moving with the key, the stack is fouled and the soak comes before the force.
steps.aside: To disassemble make sure the firearm is unloaded and remove from host firearm.
steps.quote: Using the provided tool key, remove the muzzle cap of the suppressor. Remove the breach cap.
steps.cite: BANISH 22 OWNER'S MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision or edition statement is printed in the document; the cached file is the 2025 posting. — CLEANING, printed p.6

steps.title: Soak an hour or two before anything is pushed
steps.action: Penetrating oil down the tube and over the baffles, then leave it alone for an hour or two. This is the step people skip and the reason a stack seizes: the oil is what lets the baffles come out without being driven.
steps.aside: It is recommended that the suppressor be cleaned regularly.
steps.quote: Soak the inside of the tube and baffles with a penetrating oil and let sit for 1 - 2 hours.
steps.cite: BANISH 22 OWNER'S MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision or edition statement is printed in the document; the cached file is the 2025 posting. — CLEANING, printed p.6

steps.title: ⛔ Baffles out — pushed, not hammered
steps.action: They should slide. Where they will not, BANISH's own answer is their baffle removal tool and a careful push — and the caution that comes with it is about damaging the baffles, so the force stops well before anything deforms.
steps.aside: This will result in the baffles not being able to slide out past the buildup.
steps.quote: If excessive fouling has occurred, our Baffle Remove Tool (sold separately) can be used to push the baffles out. Care must be taken to avoid damage to the baffles.
steps.cite: BANISH 22 OWNER'S MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision or edition statement is printed in the document; the cached file is the 2025 posting. — CLEANING, printed p.6

steps.title: Nylon brush, baffles and tube, until the carbon is off
steps.action: Nylon, not bronze, and not a wire wheel — the finish and the baffle faces are what you are protecting. Work the tube's inside wall as well as the baffles; the wall is where the build-up that stops the next strip actually lives.
steps.aside: Note: .22 Long rifle projectiles are not jacketed.
steps.quote: Scrub the baffles and tube with a nylon brush to remove carbon deposits.
steps.cite: BANISH 22 OWNER'S MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision or edition statement is printed in the document; the cached file is the 2025 posting. — CLEANING, printed p.6

steps.title: Dry, then a light film of oil on the baffles
steps.action: Everything dry first — oil over solvent is paste. Then the thinnest film on the baffles, which BANISH gives for one reason only: so the stack goes back together and comes apart again next time.
steps.aside: Cleaning is required every 100 - 200 rounds to avoid having the baffles fuse together.
steps.quote: Once all parts are clean and dry, add a light film of oil on the baffles, to aid in assembly
steps.cite: BANISH 22 OWNER'S MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision or edition statement is printed in the document; the cached file is the 2025 posting. — CLEANING, printed p.6

deepAbsentReason: BANISH publishes NO procedure deeper than the one above for this can, and there is nothing deeper to publish: the BANISH 22 is a tube, two caps and a stack of individual baffles, and the field strip already takes all of it apart. A baffle does not itself come apart. ⛔ The book's only escalation past its own cleaning section is to the maker — the warranty page sends a suppressor needing repair back to Customer Service — so inventing a deeper teardown would be substitution from a different product, which is the exact failure the sealed/serviceable record exists to prevent.

cleaning.name: BAFFLE STACK
tasks: Soaked 1–2 hours in penetrating oil before anything is pushed
Pushed out, never driven — BANISH's own tool where the stack resists
Nylon-brushed until the carbon is off, then dried
Light film of oil on the baffles, for assembly only

cleaning.name: TUBE
tasks: Inside wall brushed — that is where the build-up that blocks the next strip sits
Threads inside the tube cleaned before grease or anti-seize goes back on

cleaning.name: CAPS AND THREADS
tasks: Muzzle cap and breach cap cleaned and dried
Barrel threads and the can's thread mount checked clean and undamaged
⛔ No gap between barrel shoulder and thread mount, ever

cleaning.name: ⛔ THE SCHEDULE IS THE MAINTENANCE
tasks: Every 100–200 rounds, by the maker's own number
A can left past it can foul solid and refuse to come apart at all

reassembly: A little grease or anti-seize on the threads inside the tube.
Breach cap into the COUNTER-BORED short end, hand tight — if it will not shoulder, it is on the wrong end.
Baffles back in with the shortest one LAST, each aligned on its own etched line.
Muzzle cap on hand tight with the key tool.
Onto the host only with the action open and clear: threads clean, screwed down until it seats against the shoulder, hand tight.
Re-check the mount is still tight after the first few shots and periodically thereafter.
fncheck: Back together and off the gun: both caps hand tight with the key, no baffle proud of either end, and the bore clear when you look through it. On the host, the can screws down until it seats against the shoulder with NO visible gap — and then it gets checked again after the first few shots, because a thread mount that walks loose is how a baffle strike starts.
